knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Water goes in first, then the measured product at the label dilution. Adding product first causes foaming and splashback.
The bucket is kept behind the operator so that the operator does not step through the mop water or the bucket is not knocked over.
Signs stay in place until the floor is fully dry. A damp floor is still a slip hazard.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied bucket and a labelled product, the learner fills water first and adds the product to the label dilution, marking the bucket; the assessor checks the measure.
On a supplied floor section, the learner wipes the skirting and edges first, then mops from the far point toward the door, with the bucket kept behind them throughout.
The learner wrings the mop over the bucket with the bucket held between their feet, with no water spilled onto the floor.
The learner leaves warning signs in place until the supplied floor is confirmed dry by the assessor, then removes them.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Bucket marking record completed by the learner
Photo of the dry floor after signs are removed, where the site permits
stopWorkCriteria: Learner adds product to the bucket before water
Learner uses a scouring pad on a polished or unsuitable floor
Learner removes warning signs before the floor is dry
Learner mops a wet floor as though it were dry, or mops a floor type the approved procedure excludes
